definitions.explanation: The traditional Japanese art of arranging flowers, emphasizing form, balance, and harmony.

examples.japanese: {生|い}け{花|ばな}を{習|なら}っている。
{玄関|げんかん}に{生|い}け{花|ばな}を{飾|かざ}る。
examples.english: To display a flower arrangement in the entrance.

examples.japanese: {生|い}け{花|ばな}の{展覧会|てんらんかい}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to an ikebana exhibition.

notes:
{生|い}け{花|ばな} is the Japanese art of flower arrangement, one of the traditional arts alongside {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony) and {書道|しょどう} (calligraphy).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {生|い}け{花|ばな}を{習|なら}う: to learn ikebana
- {生|い}け{花|ばな}を{飾|かざ}る: to display a flower arrangement
- {生|い}け{花|ばな}の{先生|せんせい}: ikebana teacher
- {生|い}け{花|ばな}{教室|きょうしつ}: ikebana class

MAJOR SCHOOLS:
- {池坊|いけのぼう}: the oldest school (over 500 years)
- {草月流|そうげつりゅう}: modern, avant-garde style
- {小原流|おはらりゅう}: naturalistic style

ALTERNATIVE TERM:
{華道|かどう} is a more formal name for the art. {華道|かどう} emphasizes it as a "way" or discipline ({道|どう}), while {生|い}け{花|ばな} is the more common everyday term.
